# ApexYard: full content

> Your agents write the code. Your process decides what merges.

This file holds the page content of https://apexyard.ai/ in one file.
It is written in plain words. It gives no prices.
<!-- feature:pricing -->For prices and plan details, read https://apexyard.ai/pricing.<!-- /feature:pricing -->

---

# What ApexYard is

ApexYard gives your agents a team's process. Then it checks every pull request against that process.

<!-- feature:build gate readiness -->ApexYard has three products: Build, Gate and Readiness.<!-- /feature:build gate readiness -->
Keel is the shared layer under them.

| Name | What it does |
|------|--------------|
<!-- feature:build -->| Build | The open-source framework. It guides your agents. |<!-- /feature:build -->
<!-- feature:gate -->| Gate | Checks each pull request against your process. |<!-- /feature:gate -->
<!-- feature:readiness -->| Readiness | Measures each repository. |<!-- /feature:readiness -->
| Keel | Your team's rules and context, read by every agent. |

## One process, three places

You write a rule one time. Then the rule works in three places:

<!-- feature:build -->1. Build guides your agent with the rule.<!-- /feature:build -->
<!-- feature:gate -->2. Gate checks each pull request against the rule.<!-- /feature:gate -->
<!-- feature:readiness -->3. Readiness measures the whole repository against the rule.<!-- /feature:readiness -->

A miss becomes a new rule. Then the loop starts again.

Example: the rule says "Every API endpoint checks who is calling." Your team adds it to its handbook and marks it blocking.
<!-- feature:build -->Build: before an agent writes code, it loads your rules. It writes each new endpoint with an auth check.<!-- /feature:build -->
<!-- feature:gate -->Gate: Rex, the review agent, checks each pull request against the rule. A blocking rule that fails stops the merge.<!-- /feature:gate -->
<!-- feature:readiness -->Readiness: the readiness audit fails when a user-facing app has no authentication.<!-- /feature:readiness -->

## Works with

<!-- feature:build -->Build works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi and omp.<!-- /feature:build -->

---

<!-- feature:build -->
<!-- feature:build --># Build (https://apexyard.ai/build)<!-- /feature:build -->

<!-- feature:build -->Build is the open-source framework. Your agents plan before they code. Every change meets a reviewer before it leaves your machine.<!-- /feature:build -->

<!-- feature:build -->Build is for founders and engineering leads who want agent speed and a real process.<!-- /feature:build -->

<!-- feature:build -->## What Build does<!-- /feature:build -->

- It turns an idea into a spec, a plan and small tickets. A person signs off each step.
- It adds reviewer roles. Code, security, architecture and QA reviewers each check what they know best. They say what to fix.
- It works with an existing repository or a new one. For an existing repository, it adds handbooks and agent guidance in place. For a new product, you start from an empty folder.
- It runs on your machine. The framework and the command line run where your developers already work.

## Licence and cost

<!-- feature:build -->- Build is open source under the MIT licence.<!-- /feature:build -->
- Rules, roles, handbooks and hooks are plain files. You can read them, change them or remove them.
<!-- feature:build -->- Build needs no account and no dashboard.<!-- /feature:build -->

## Install

The hooks are Bash scripts. On macOS and Linux, Bash is there already. On Windows, use Git Bash or WSL.

1. Install the command line tool: `brew install me2resh/tap/apexyard && apexyard init`. The command asks for the name and the account. Or run `npx create-apexyard --org <your-org> --name <new-private-repo> --private`.
2. You need git. `apexyard doctor` checks for jq and the GitHub CLI (gh) and tells you how to install what is missing.
3. Open the new folder in your coding agent and run /setup.

The install guide is at https://apexyard.ai/docs.

<!-- feature:build gate -->## How Build connects to Gate<!-- /feature:build gate -->

<!-- feature:build gate -->The ticket, the decision record and the review that your agents make in Build are what Gate checks on GitHub.<!-- /feature:build gate -->

<!-- /feature:build -->

<!-- feature:cockpit -->
<!-- feature:cockpit --># Cockpit (https://apexyard.ai/cockpit)<!-- /feature:cockpit -->

<!-- feature:build cockpit -->Cockpit is a preview of the desktop app for Build. It is not a fourth product. [Preview]<!-- /feature:build cockpit -->

<!-- feature:gate -->- What works today: a setup panel, governed runs that stop at each gate, a run view, a needs-you panel, and an ORBIT planning view.<!-- /feature:gate -->
- Known limit: sign-in with your ApexYard account is off. [Planned]
- Known limit: a governed run can call gh with your GitHub login, and that login can merge pull requests.
<!-- feature:build -->- How to get it: there is no download yet. Today you build it from source, and you need access to the source repository. Write to us to ask for access.<!-- /feature:build -->

<!-- /feature:cockpit -->

<!-- feature:gate -->
<!-- feature:gate --># Gate (https://apexyard.ai/gate)<!-- /feature:gate -->

<!-- feature:gate -->Gate checks each pull request against your process. Each merge needs a passing check and the approval of a person your team names.<!-- /feature:gate -->

<!-- feature:gate -->Gate is for engineering leads whose teams merge code that agents wrote.<!-- /feature:gate -->

<!-- feature:gate -->## What Gate does<!-- /feature:gate -->

- It puts the result in the checks of the pull request. The result shows what passed, what is missing and the next step. [Early teams (by hand)]
- It checks four things: a linked ticket, a decision record, a review and a named approval.
- An agent never approves its own work. By default, reviewers run on a stronger model than builders (checked on 10 November 2026 in the agent files of the framework). With named approval set up, the merge waits for a person that your team named. [Early teams (by hand)]
- You can export the record of each merge for an auditor. [Planned]
- It shows every open change on one screen. You see what each pull request is missing and who holds it up. [Early teams (by hand)]
- The organisation view shows which pull requests skipped a step, in every repository. [Early teams (by hand)]

<!-- feature:gate -->Gate blocks a merge only when you make the check required in GitHub.<!-- /feature:gate -->

<!-- feature:gate -->Each hosted part has one label: Available now, Early teams (by hand), or Planned with its date. The hosted Gate runs by hand for early teams today.<!-- /feature:gate -->

## What the GitHub App can see

Our servers never fetch your code. The App has no Contents permission. From each pull request it takes the title, the description and the names of the changed files.

- Pull requests: read. Titles, descriptions, reviews and the list of changed files.
- Checks: write. The App posts the ApexYard check on each pull request.
- Metadata: read. Repository names, and who can write to each repository.
- Members: read. Who belongs to your organisation.

Checked on 10 November 2026 with the GitHub API: the App holds these four permissions and no others.

You can remove the App at any time.

<!-- feature:build gate -->## How Gate connects to Build<!-- /feature:build gate -->

<!-- feature:build gate -->Gate checks the ticket, the decision record and the review that your agents make in Build.<!-- /feature:build gate -->

---

<!-- /feature:gate -->

<!-- feature:readiness -->
<!-- feature:readiness --># Readiness (https://apexyard.ai/readiness)<!-- /feature:readiness -->

<!-- feature:readiness -->Readiness measures each repository. It tells you if the repository is ready for production, area by area.<!-- /feature:readiness -->

<!-- feature:readiness -->Readiness is for CTOs and engineering leads who answer for what ships.<!-- /feature:readiness -->

<!-- feature:readiness -->## What Readiness does<!-- /feature:readiness -->

<!-- feature:readiness -->Readiness runs one audit on a repository. The audit has ten areas:<!-- /feature:readiness -->

- security
- accessibility
- compliance
- analytics
- search
- AI search
- performance
- monitoring
- documentation
- behaviour quality

You get a go or no-go, the gaps in each area and the top actions.

<!-- feature:build readiness -->## How Readiness connects to Build<!-- /feature:build readiness -->

<!-- feature:build -->Turn a finding into a rule. Your agents pick up the rule on their next ticket in Build.<!-- /feature:build -->

---

<!-- /feature:readiness -->

# Keel

Keel is the name for your team's rules and context. Every agent reads it.

<!-- feature:build gate readiness -->The rules that you write one time live in Keel. Build uses them to guide your agents. Gate uses them to check pull requests. Readiness uses them to measure repositories.<!-- /feature:build gate readiness -->
